paragraphs.text: Cornelia de Lange syndrome-4 (CDLS4) is a cohesinopathy caused by mutation in the gene for the cohesin structural protein RAD21. Affected individuals have growth retardation, minor skeletal anomalies, and facial features that overlap those of classic Cornelia de Lange syndrome (CdLS), but cognitive impairment is milder than in CdLS caused by mutation in NIPBL, SMC1A, or SMC3 (Deardorff et al., 2012). Compared with NIPBL- and SMC1A-related CdLS, the phenotype is attenuated for facial morphology, limb anomalies, and especially cognition and behavior; some patients have holoprosencephaly, with or without CdLS features, and variants are frequently familial with marked intra- and interfamilial variability (Krab et al., 2020).

paragraphs.text: Krab et al. (2020) assembled a series of 49 individuals from 33 families with RAD21 alterations, including 24 previously unpublished cases; full clinical data were available for 29 individuals (22 families; cohort A; age range 0-61 years, median 9 years). All cohort A patients had CdLS clinical scores of at least 5, and CdLS had been suspected before testing in 13 of 21 index cases in whom this was specified. Most CdLS features were present but at lower frequency and severity than in NIPBL and SMC1A cohorts: major limb malformations were not seen (0/29), hands and feet were generally of normal size, and hirsutism was less frequent (38%). Frequent features included short nose (88%), long and/or smooth philtrum (90%), concave nasal ridge (83%), thick eyebrows (83%), long eyelashes (81%), short fifth finger (82%), and postnatal microcephaly (57%). Growth at birth was generally less impaired, with short stature and microcephaly developing postnatally. Hearing loss was found in 8 of 24, cardiac anomalies in 9 of 23, gastroesophageal reflux (typically mild) in 13 of 25, and seizures in 2 of 22. Unusual anomalies included vertebral clefts and hemivertebrae and malformations of foregut-derived structures. Sixteen of 29 (55%) had normal or mildly impaired cognition, none had severe or profound disability, and all aged 3 years and above used some words. Behavioral problems, mainly anxiety, ADHD, autism spectrum features, and obsessive-compulsive behavior, were present in 14 of 25; self-injurious behavior and aggression were uncommon. Intrafamilial variability, especially in cognition and behavior, was considerable, and some mildly affected parents were diagnosed only after recognition of more severely affected offspring.

paragraphs.text: In a 15-month-old boy with CDLS4 and diaphragmatic hernia, Gudmundsson et al. (2019) identified a de novo 3-bp deletion (c.1774_1776del) in the RAD21 gene, resulting in deletion of gln592. The variant was found by exome sequencing and was absent in both healthy parents. Structural modeling predicted disruption of the RAD21-SMC1A interface. Krab et al. (2020) found by molecular dynamics that the deletion displaces lys605 away from ATPase site 1.

checks.claim: Gudmundsson et al. (2019) reported a 15-month-old boy with CDLS4.
checks.evidence_quote: we report a patient that expands the clinical description of CdLS type 4
checks.explanation: The patient is the 15-month-old boy described in the abstract.

checks.claim: The 15-month-old boy with CDLS4 reported by Gudmundsson et al. (2019) had a diaphragmatic hernia.
checks.evidence_quote: prominent digit pads and diaphragmatic hernia

checks.claim: Gudmundsson et al. (2019) identified a 3-bp deletion (c.1774_1776del) in the RAD21 gene in a 15-month-old boy with CDLS4.
checks.evidence_quote: Exome sequencing revealed a novel RAD21 variant, c.1774_1776del, p.(Gln592del), suggestive of CdLS type 4.

checks.claim: The RAD21 c.1774_1776del deletion results in deletion of gln592.
checks.explanation: The abstract gives the protein effect as p.(Gln592del), a deletion of gln592.

checks.claim: The RAD21 c.1774_1776del deletion was found by exome sequencing.
checks.evidence_quote: Exome sequencing revealed a novel RAD21 variant, c.1774_1776del

checks.claim: The RAD21 c.1774_1776del deletion was de novo, being absent in both parents of the patient.
checks.evidence_quote: Segregation analysis of the two healthy parents confirmed the variant as de novo
checks.explanation: A de novo result from testing both parents means neither parent carried the variant.

checks.claim: Both parents of the boy with the RAD21 c.1774_1776del deletion were healthy.
checks.evidence_quote: Segregation analysis of the two healthy parents confirmed the variant as de novo
checks.explanation: The abstract describes both parents as healthy.

checks.claim: Structural modeling predicted that the RAD21 gln592 deletion disrupts the RAD21-SMC1A interface.
checks.evidence_quote: a novel RAD21 p.(Glu592del) variant that causes a disturbed RAD21-SMC1A interface according to in silco structural modeling
checks.explanation: Stated in the abstract. The 'Glu592' here is a typo in the abstract, which elsewhere says Gln592.

checks.claim: Molecular dynamics showed that the RAD21 gln592 deletion displaces lys605 away from ATPase site 1.
checks.evidence_quote: This situation promotes a conformational change in the alpha helix, causing the Lys605, which is placed in the same alpha helix, to move away from site 1 of the ATPase.

agent.process_note: I opened all 10 papers. Only Krab et al. (2020) was available in full text, and I read all of it, including Tables 1-3. The other 8 were abstracts only, and Goel and Parasivam (2020) was a title only, so I cited it just for what the title says. Abstracts do not give the specific variants or inheritance for the patients of Deardorff (2012), Kruszka (2019) or Dorval (2020). For those I relied on Krab's Table 1 and say so in the text each time. Some things are missing from the evidence: the exact number of Deardorff patients and their individual phenotypes, and how many of Kruszka's 4 non-X-linked cases carried RAD21 variants. Krab's text writes Pro367Arg, but its Table 1 and figure legend give c.1127C>G/p.(Pro376Arg), so I used P376R. The gene MIM number (606462) and the 8q24 location come from Krab et al. (2020), because no reference data was supplied. I did not create allelic variants for the biallelic A622T variant (Mungan syndrome) or the other variants that Krab tabulates only briefly.
